title: Loop Dropout: Regularizing Shared Updates in Looped Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2609.34218v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Looped language models separate computational depth from parameter count by repeatedly applying the same transformer block. Adapting these models requires a shared update that remains effective as hidden states evolve throughout the recurrent computation. Our empirical analysis reveals a pronounced late-loop bias in standard low-rank adaptation (LoRA): the shared update provides limited adaptation at early loop positions. This imbalance motivates training shared updates under varying combinations of their applications. Randomly omitting adapter applications alone, however, does not improve task performance; it reduces expected update strength during training while leaving inference unchanged. We introduce Loop Dropout, which couples stochastic masking of adapter applications with inverse-survival rescaling to preserve expected update strength and promote effective adaptation across loops. translated_title: Loop Dropout：循环语言模型中共享更新的正则化方法
translated_abstract: 循环语言模型通过反复应用相同的Transformer块，将计算深度与参数量解耦。适配这类模型需要一个共享更新，使其在循环计算中隐状态不断演化的过程中保持有效。我们的实证分析表明，标准的低秩适配（LoRA）存在明显的后期循环偏差：共享更新在早期循环位置的适配效果十分有限。这一不平衡现象促使我们在共享更新应用的不同组合下对其进行训练。然而，仅仅随机省略适配器的应用并不能提升任务性能，因为它在训练期间降低了预期的更新强度，而推理过程保持不变。我们提出了Loop Dropout，该方法将适配器应用的随机掩码与逆生存重缩放相结合，以保持预期的更新强度，并促进整个循环过程中的有效适配。大量实验证明了改进……
tldr: 提出Loop Dropout方法，通过将适配器应用的随机掩码与逆生存重缩放相结合，解决了循环语言模型中LoRA在早期循环位置适配不足的后期循环偏差问题，在保持预期更新强度的同时实现循环全过程的有效适配。
en_tdlr: Loop Dropout addresses the late-loop bias of standard LoRA in looped language models by coupling stochastic masking of adapter applications with inverse-survival rescaling, preserving expected update strength and enabling effective adaptation across all recurrent loops.
